topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Traditional cancer therapies and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional local and systemic cancer treatments—such as surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—alongside the challenges of systemic toxicity and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic vulnerabilities of cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Kinase-targeted therapies and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale and mechanisms for inhibiting oncogenic kinases along with the evolutionary resistance pathways and dosing strategies that arise during treatment.

topics.label: Therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates specifically target tumor-associated cell-surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and immune-mediated targeting
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address immune surveillance and cell-mediated immunotherapies designed to harness or engineer T cells to target cancer.

topics.label: Overall progress, systemic challenges, and future perspectives in cancer care
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader progress, persistent clinical challenges, and future paradigms across cancer prevention, treatment combinations, and drug development.
